title: A structure-guided approach to noncoding variant evaluation for transcription factor binding using AlphaFold 3.
authors: Gerasimavicius, Lukas; Biddie, Simon C; Marsh, Joseph A
one_liner_zh: 该文利用AlphaFold 3建模TF-DNA复合物并结合FoldX能量评估，系统预测非编码SNV对转录因子结合的影响，核心聚焦TF-DNA互作机制与结构建模，方法上融合AI结构预测与物理能量分析，高度匹配本课题。
abstract: Noncoding single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) that alter transcription factor (TF) binding can affect gene expression and contribute to disease. Sequence-based methods can excel at predicting TF binding, but rely on training data and can exhibit TF-specific biases. Here, we propose a structure-guided approach for noncoding SNVs, using AlphaFold 3 (AF3) to model TF-DNA complexes and FoldX for downstream physics-based assessment. Benchmarked against single nucleotide polymorphism-systematic evolution of ligands by exponential enrichment (SNP-SELEX) data for six TFs (SPIB, ELK3, ETV4, SF-1, PAX5, and MEIS2), the FoldX-based strategy showed good agreement with experimental allele preferences. Interestingly, differences in AF3's interface-predicted template modelling (ipTM) score aligned even more closely with SNP-SELEX results, generally surpassing energy-based metrics. Application to known disease-associated variants recapitulated most reported effects for TFs including NKX2-5, GATA3, and USF2A-USF1. In these examples, considering both DeltaipTM and FoldX energies proved more reliable than either metric alone. While less accurate than state-of-the-art sequence-based methods, this work demonstrates that structural modelling can yield interpretable insights into how noncoding variants influence TF binding. By highlighting both the promise and limitations of AF3 in this context, our study provides a framework for complementary structural evaluation of regulatory variants.
abstract_zh: 改变转录因子（TF）结合的非编码单核苷酸变异（SNVs）可影响基因表达并导致疾病。基于序列的方法在预测TF结合方面表现出色，但依赖训练数据，并可能呈现TF特异性偏差。在此，我们提出一种结构引导的非编码SNVs分析方法，利用AlphaFold 3（AF3）建模TF-DNA复合物，并结合FoldX进行下游基于物理学的评估。以六个TF（SPIB、ELK3、ETV4、SF-1、PAX5和MEIS2）的单核苷酸多态性-指数富集配体系统进化（SNP-SELEX）数据为基准，基于FoldX的策略与实验等位基因偏好表现出良好一致性。有趣的是，AF3界面预测模板建模（ipTM）评分的差异与SNP-SELEX结果更为吻合，通常优于基于能量的指标。应用于已知疾病相关变异时，该方法重现了包括NKX2-5、GATA3和USF2A-USF1在内的TF的大多数已报道效应。在这些例子中，结合DeltaipTM和FoldX能量比单独使用任一指标更为可靠。尽管不如最先进的基于序列的方法准确，但本研究证明结构建模能为非编码变异如何影响TF结合提供可解释的见解。通过强调AF3在此背景下的潜力和局限性，我们的研究为调控变异的互补结构评估提供了一个框架。
